channel.title: esm.business
channel.description: Relevant news on agentic AI, ESM around ServiceNow, digital sovereignty and tech in practice.

item.title: AOK Plus deploys AI agents and EU cloud in member services
item.description:
German health insurer AOK Plus has rolled out a cloud-based AI platform with around 120 skills for 2,400 staff, handling requests from 3.5 million members in Saxony and Thuringia. A voice assistant answers routine questions around the clock, while complex cases go to staff. AOK Plus reports a 95% call acceptance rate, run on an EU sovereign cloud.
Why it matters Shows how a large statutory health insurer runs AI agents at scale in production while relying on an EU cloud for data protection – relevant to sovereignty and scaling questions in healthcare.
Source: CIO.de

item.title: DKB automates email processing in customer service with AI
item.description:
Deutsche Kreditbank (DKB) has introduced an AI assistant built on the Pega platform for its roughly 1,500 service staff, automatically summarizing incoming customer emails and suggesting replies. Staff still decide on next steps. The system covers millions of emails from the bank's more than 5.5 million customers.
Why it matters Illustrates a production use of AI agents with human-in-the-loop oversight in a German bank's customer service – relevant to governance questions around steering semi-autonomous agents.
Source: CIO.de

item.title: Bitkom/IDC: German companies raise AI spending 48% in 2026
item.description:
According to a Bitkom/IDC survey, German companies will spend around €28.7bn on AI in 2026, up 48% from €19.4bn in 2025. Spending on generative AI doubles to €11.5bn, and a further rise to €40.3bn is expected for 2027.
Why it matters Provides hard figures for the shift from AI pilots to broad production use across German companies of all industries.
Source: CIO.de

item.title: Google reportedly withheld disclosure of AI agent security incident, WSJ says
item.description:
Per the Wall Street Journal, an AI agent based on Google's Gemini model breached three simulated target companies in a test by security firm Irregular, guessing credentials or finding them exposed online. Google disclosed the incident only after press inquiries; agents from Anthropic, OpenAI and Meta reportedly had similar incidents in comparable tests.
Why it matters Highlights real security risks of autonomous AI agents and raises disclosure and governance questions for all major AI vendors.
Source: Computerwoche

item.title: Bitkom survey: shadow AI use rising noticeably in German companies
item.description:
According to a Bitkom survey, 8% of German companies say private AI tools are used widely and without central control internally, double the 4% recorded a year earlier. A further 17% suspect this is the case without being certain.
Why it matters Uncontrolled AI use by employees is becoming a growing governance and data-protection risk for security teams.
Source: CIO.de

item.title: Real-world test: nine employees manage over 100 AI agents in a company
item.description:
The report describes a nine-person team testing how to manage and scale more than 100 AI agents as digital staff. The focus is on the leadership structures needed to keep an agent fleet this size reliable.
Why it matters A practical example of managing large agent fleets – shows what leadership and control structures agentic AI needs at scale.
Source: Handelsblatt

item.title: Germany and Canada fund AI safety project LawZero, with a Berlin site
item.description:
Germany plans around €100m, Canada up to CA$150m in funding for LawZero, the non-profit AI safety project led by Turing laureate Yoshua Bengio. Its "Scientist AI" concept is a safety-oriented alternative to autonomous AI agents; the project is opening a new Berlin site, with 360 full-time jobs planned in Canada.
Why it matters State funding for independent, safety-focused AI research with a German site – relevant to the debate on AI and digital sovereignty.
Source: heise online

item.title: Study: data protection rules haven't held back AI innovation in Germany
item.description:
A position paper from Fraunhofer ISI and the University of Kassel ("Plattform Privatheit" project) challenges the claim that less data protection means more AI innovation. Instead of blanket deregulation, the authors call for targeted relief for start-ups and SMEs and obligations tied to actual processing risk.
Why it matters Provides arguments for the ongoing debate on simplifying GDPR and the AI Act – relevant for anyone shaping compliance requirements.
Source: CIO.de

item.title: Agentic AI Hub: AI agents cut processing times over 90% in 19 German municipalities
item.description:
In the federal Agentic AI Hub, 19 municipalities and nine AI start-ups ran 20 pilot projects for AI agents in public administration. Processing times for complex applications fell by over 90%, and 95% of municipalities were satisfied. A second three-month pilot phase started on 7 September.
Why it matters Shows with solid figures how AI agents can speed up administrative processes – a reference case for governance and scaling of agents in the public sector.
Source: BMDS

item.title: Lünendonk study: banks rarely make the leap from AI pilot to production
item.description:
A Lünendonk study finds 58% of banks are piloting AI agents, but only 19% run them live for single tasks and just 1% end-to-end across core processes. At 66% of firms, fewer than a quarter of pilots reached production.
Why it matters Shows how wide the gap between AI announcements and real ESM production still is in financial services – useful for expectation management on agentic AI projects.
Source: IT Finanzmagazin

item.title: AI paradox: 60% of German firms use agents, only 5% redesign workflows
item.description:
A survey finds 60% of German companies already use AI agents, yet only 5% have fundamentally adapted their workflows. Cited brakes are missing expertise, security concerns and unchanged processes.
Why it matters Shows that adopting tools alone isn't enough – without process and governance changes, the benefit of AI agents stays limited.
Source: Born City

item.title: Salesforce outage during Dreamforce exposes cloud-dependency risk
item.description:
Salesforce suffered roughly seven and a half hours of downtime during its own Dreamforce event. The incident highlights how dependent companies are on the availability of individual cloud platforms.
Why it matters A reminder that resilience and multi-vendor strategies matter for any ESM or CRM platform – not only ServiceNow.
Source: Computerwoche

item.title: Digital ministry backs market-ready tech and secure AI with up to €5m
item.description:
Germany's federal digital ministry is backing small and mid-sized firms with up to €5m to bring digital innovations to market readiness, while also advancing joint secure-AI standards with Canada.
Why it matters Shows concrete funding routes for sovereign tech and AI projects in Germany – relevant for vendors and customers relying on state support.
Source: heise online

item.title: LinkedIn, IBM and DoorDash lift dev productivity 20% with AI agents
item.description:
LinkedIn, IBM, DoorDash and other companies are running AI agents in production for development, testing and maintenance – mostly under human oversight. LinkedIn puts the productivity gain in software development at 20%.
Why it matters A concrete example of AI agents in production in software development – with human oversight rather than full autonomy.
Source: Born City

item.title: AI agent as pentester: VORNAC claims over 97% attack-surface coverage
item.description:
VORNAC's AI agent already runs in production, including at a large German insurer. The vendor claims over 97% attack-surface coverage, versus 5–20% for classic pentests.
Why it matters Shows how AI agents can run in production in security-critical processes – with human follow-up rather than black-box automation.
Source: Computerwoche

item.title: Telekom uses Mistral on T Cloud for call notes
item.description:
'Voice AI Notes' summarises business calls with the Mistral Small 4 model and processes data in European data centres. From 2027, calls are to trigger tasks, CRM entries or service tickets automatically.
Why it matters Sovereign AI moves from pilot to standard product – and ends up directly in a service ticket. Interfaces to ESM platforms become a sovereignty issue.
Source: Deutsche Telekom

item.title: T-Systems: one control centre for many AI agents
item.description:
With the T-AI Agentic Hub, Telekom offers a platform to run many agents under control. Banco Sabadell plans to use it to embed agentic AI across the group and improve the experience of about seven million customers.
Why it matters Agent control towers are becoming their own product category – with European vendors competing on sovereignty.
Source: Deutsche Telekom

item.title: How much should an AI agent decide on its own?
item.description:
T-Systems' CTO AI & Data recommends starting with an agent for a narrow, verifiable task. Once agents in several areas access different systems, identities, permissions, traceability, security and human approvals must be designed in from the start.
Why it matters A good template for an autonomy matrix: which tasks an agent handles alone, with approval, or not at all.
Source: Deutsche Telekom

item.title: Build Agent now self-updates, IDE merges into Studio
item.description:
The September store release for Otto for Creator runs on Zurich Patch 12 and Australia Patch 6. Manual Build Agent upgrades are gone and the ServiceNow IDE is merged into Studio. Brazil Early Availability follows on 24 September.
Why it matters Move development guidelines and code review to Studio; keep securing AI-generated code with ATF.
Source: ServiceNow Community

item.title: Atos to resell and integrate STACKIT
item.description:
Atos and Schwarz Digits signed a partnership in Munich: Atos will resell the STACKIT platform and integrate it into client landscapes.
Why it matters Sovereign clouds are going mainstream through large integrators. Service management must cover hybrid landscapes with US and EU platforms.
Source: Dr. Web Magazin

item.title: Swiss federal administration launches openDesk programme
item.description:
According to the Federal Chancellery, the federal administration's digital workplace can in principle run on open-source software. From the end of 2027, around 3,000 staff in particularly critical processes are to use email, calendar, documents and video conferencing based on openDesk; the first phase is estimated at CHF 9m.
Why it matters ESM processes will need to connect to sovereign workplace suites too, not just Microsoft 365.
Source: Schweizerische Bundeskanzlei

item.title: AI Control Tower as registry and cost control
item.description:
MCP servers are registered and monitored as AI assets in the AI Control Tower inventory. ServiceNow says costs can be tracked per department, agents switched off and cheaper models chosen per task.
Why it matters Register agents from other platforms there too, or shadow AI grows beside the platform.
Source: ServiceNow Docs

item.title: Retail: agents planned, customers still hesitant
item.description:
In an EHI survey of German-speaking retailers, 11.6% already use agentic commerce applications and 48.4% plan to. 22.8% run a shopping assistant. The sample is not representative.
Why it matters Retail invests at the customer front first. Returns, store service and supplier processes behind it must catch up, or the service chain will slow the agent down.
Source: etailment

item.title: ServiceNow AI passes $1bn in annual contract value
item.description:
According to ServiceNow, its AI business passed $1bn in annual contract value for the first time in Q2 2026. Agentic deployments grew ninefold within nine months.
Why it matters The debate shifts from 'whether' to 'how do we govern cost and value' – consumption pricing makes it more urgent.
Source: ServiceNow Newsroom

item.title: Raleigh cuts IT service desk cost by 66%
item.description:
According to ServiceNow, the city of Raleigh, North Carolina, now routes 98% of tickets correctly on the first attempt using AI agents. That cuts IT service desk cost by 66% and frees up more than 1,300 staff hours a year.
Why it matters A strong public-sector figure – but as a vendor claim only comparable with the baseline in view.
Source: ServiceNow

item.title: CMDB MCP Server: CMDB access for external AI clients
item.description:
In the Australia release ServiceNow exposes CMDB functions such as search, CI creation and class suggestions as MCP tools. External AI clients use them without direct database access; access via OAuth and the roles sn_cmdb_user or sn_cmdb_editor.
Why it matters Limit agent write access deliberately and model agents as separate machine identities.
Source: ServiceNow Docs

item.title: McKinsey: large firms scale agents – returns not yet following
item.description:
Among companies with more than $1bn in revenue, 40% already scale AI agents, up from 27% a year earlier. Around a fifth say model operating costs limit their use.
Why it matters Scale alone does not deliver returns. Cost per agent and process becomes a key control metric.
Source: brutkasten

item.title: Fraunhofer: AI assistant for discharge letters
item.description:
Fraunhofer IAIS developed an assistant that analyses history, findings and test results and turns them into standardised letter formats. One participating clinic writes around 2,500 discharge letters a year.
Why it matters Documentation is the biggest quick lever in health care. Physician review remains mandatory and must be visible in the process.
Source: Fraunhofer IAIS

item.title: Telekom automates entire service chains for business customers
item.description:
An agent turns a fault report into a ticket, then a technician appointment and finally an invoice – with no phone call in between. It builds on partnerships with n8n and Parloa; complex cases stay with people.
Why it matters The benchmark moves from chatbots to end-to-end automation. That is where it becomes clear whether service platforms and agents work together cleanly.
Source: digital-magazin.de

item.title: Mercedes-Benz scales AI across its workforce
item.description:
Mercedes wants employees to shape AI, not just use it, and defines three competence levels. At the top, business teams build their own workflows, for example with n8n. A hackathon with more than 1,500 employees accelerated the rollout.
Why it matters Automation is moving into business teams. That speeds things up but quickly creates parallel workflow worlds that someone has to hold together.
Source: Computerwoche
